topics.name: Regression
topics.description: A statistical method for modeling the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables.

sub_topics.name: Linear Regression
sub_topics.description: A type of regression analysis that models the relationship using a linear equation.

sub_topics.name: Logistic Regression
sub_topics.description: A regression model used for binary classification tasks.

sub_topics.name: Ridge Regression
sub_topics.description: A technique used to analyze multiple regression data that suffer from multicollinearity.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and algebra.
common_misconceptions: Only linear relationships can be modeled
practical_applications: Predicting sales based on advertising spend
Estimating housing prices based on features

topics.name: Statistical Learning
topics.description: A framework for understanding and applying statistical methods to learn from data.

sub_topics.name: Model Selection
sub_topics.description: The process of selecting a statistical model from a set of candidate models.

sub_topics.name: Hypothesis Testing
sub_topics.description: A method for testing a hypothesis about a parameter in a statistical model.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and probability.
common_misconceptions: Statistical learning is only about regression.
More data always leads to better models.

topics.name: Neural Networks
topics.description: Computational models inspired by the human brain, used for various machine learning tasks.

sub_topics.name: Artificial Neural Network
sub_topics.description: A network of algorithms that attempts to recognize underlying relationships in a set of data.

sub_topics.name: Activation Function
sub_topics.description: A mathematical function that determines the output of a neural network node.

sub_topics.name: Backpropagation
sub_topics.description: An algorithm for training neural networks by minimizing the error.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of linear algebra and calculus, familiarity with programming concepts.
common_misconceptions: Neural networks can learn without data
More layers always mean better performance

topics.name: Support Vector Machines
topics.description: A supervised learning model used for classification and regression analysis.

sub_topics.name: Hyperplane
sub_topics.description: A decision boundary that separates different classes in a support vector machine.

sub_topics.name: Margin
sub_topics.description: The distance between the hyperplane and the nearest data point from either class.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of linear algebra and statistics.
common_misconceptions: SVMs can only be used for linear classification
More support vectors always lead to better models

topics.name: Clustering
topics.description: A method of grouping a set of objects in such a way that objects in the same group are more similar than those in other groups.

sub_topics.name: Hierarchical Clustering
sub_topics.description: A method of cluster analysis that seeks to build a hierarchy of clusters.

sub_topics.name: K-Means Clustering
sub_topics.description: A partitioning method that divides a dataset into K distinct non-overlapping subsets.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and linear algebra.
common_misconceptions: Clustering is the same as classification
All clustering algorithms produce the same results

topics.name: Model Evaluation
topics.description: The process of assessing the performance of a machine learning model.

sub_topics.name: Error Rate
sub_topics.description: The proportion of incorrect predictions made by a model.

sub_topics.name: Model Accuracy
sub_topics.description: The ratio of correctly predicted instances to the total instances.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of machine learning concepts and algorithms.
common_misconceptions: Higher accuracy always means a better model
Overfitting is not a concern if the model performs well on training data

topics.name: Survival Analysis
topics.description: A set of statistical approaches for data analysis where the outcome variable is the time until an event occurs.

sub_topics.name: Survival Function
sub_topics.description: A function that estimates the probability of survival beyond a certain time.

sub_topics.name: Hazard Function
sub_topics.description: A function that describes the instantaneous risk of the event occurring.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and probability, familiarity with regression analysis.
common_misconceptions: Survival analysis only applies to medical data
Time-to-event data must be normally distributed

topics.name: Regression Trees
topics.description: A decision tree that predicts a continuous value based on input features.

sub_topics.name: Decision Trees
sub_topics.description: A flowchart-like structure used for classification and regression.

sub_topics.name: Regression Splines
sub_topics.description: A flexible method for fitting a regression model using piecewise polynomial functions.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and decision trees.
common_misconceptions: Regression trees can only predict linear relationships
More splits always lead to better predictions

topics.name: Predictors
topics.description: Variables that are used to predict the outcome of a dependent variable.

sub_topics.name: Predictor Variables
sub_topics.description: Independent variables used in regression models.

sub_topics.name: Coefficients
sub_topics.description: Values that represent the relationship between predictors and the response variable.

summary.prerequisites_summary: Basic understanding of statistics and algebra.
common_misconceptions: More predictors always lead to better predictions
